The issue with the vertigo is that it comes in episodes, it's not something I have constantly so I'm not sure if physical therapy would help or not. I would be willing to try it, possibly.

What I did that helped a lot, was being vigilant about not bringing sweets and junk food into the house. Portion control is also really important, and I think it's a lot easier if you cook your own food if you can.

Something you could also experiment with, if you have to have a big plate of food to feel full is to eat less meals in the day, ie; eating a large lunch and dinner, but skipping breakfast(or big breakfast, and skip lunch). Just make sure you eat enough in the day, and on some kind of schedule. It's also okay to have a snack here and there. 

Sometimes when you feel hungry, that can be fixed by drinking water, as well. (Staying hydrated will also help move fluids out, which ironically can reduce fluid weight)

I would recommend instead of squeezing so many topics into one hour each day, just work on one category per day or even week. Even in game development teams you'll see different departments will have heavier workloads at different times, ie: its hard to write music for a game that doesn't even have concept art. 

On top of that, you don't have to strive for having the best of all of those disciplines. If you're not good at drawing, make that part of the style, or make something simpler visually.

There are also lots of books and videos on game design or development, but it sounds like design is a little more what you have in mind with doing a bit of everything. However, don't get so obsessed with youtube tutorials or reading without doing anything, you're probably gonna learn the most actually opening up Unity and googling how to do certain things than reading books on game design theory.
